profile.name: Md Mushfiqur Rahman
profile.title: PhD Candidate, Computer Science
profile.objective: I am a final year PhD candidate at George Mason University specializing in NLP and its applications in health, with a Master's degree in Computer Science (Machine Learning concentration) and a strong background in Mathematics. My research focuses on improving information accessibility in the healthcare domain and investigating how tone and dialect variations impact the robustness of large language models. I have interned at Amazon as an Applied Scientist and at the US Naval Research Laboratory, where I built a GAN-based image denoiser now actively used in the Hinode spacecraft. I have published 10 peer-reviewed papers, including 3 in top-tier journals, and am seeking research and industry positions at the intersection of NLP, healthcare AI, and LLM robustness.

projects.title: LLM Robustness - Multi-turn Jailbreaking (ATTCK-R)
projects.description: Developed two novel approaches — iterative tactic curation and informed traceback — for multi-turn LLM jailbreaking evaluation. Tactic curation increases attack success rate by 16% while informed traceback reduces cost by 12%, establishing a new framework for vulnerability detection in AI systems.

projects.title: SPQA - Style Perturbations on QA Capabilities of LLMs
projects.description: Introduced SPQA, a novel evaluation framework to test the robustness of LLMs under style perturbations. Key finding: stylistic changes lead to measurable performance degradation even when semantic intent is fully preserved during perturbation — revealing a critical vulnerability in current LLM deployments.

projects.title: Health Information Simplification and Summarization
projects.description: Created a parallel text dataset for health-text simplification in collaboration with nurse practitioners and patient-communication experts. Fine-tuned GPT-4 and Llama-2 (with PPO and RLHF) to achieve SOTA results. Trained Llama-2 with 16-bit quantized Q-LoRA, minimizing GPU usage by 60% and training time by 90%.

projects.title: Dialectal toxicity detection: Evaluating LLM-as-a-judge consistency across language varieties
projects.description: Evaluated the consistency of LLMs as judges for toxicity detection across different dialects of a language. Found significant inconsistencies in LLM judgments across dialects, highlighting the need for more robust and inclusive evaluation frameworks in multilingual NLP applications.

projects.title: Cross-lingual Transfer: Tokenization vs Non-tokenization
projects.description: Compared tokenization-based models (BERT, mBERT) with tokenization-free models (PIXEL, CANINE) across 19 source and 133 target languages for 3 common NLP tasks. Proposed a decision aid for text-representation selection, underscoring the importance of non-tokenization models for specific tasks.

projects.title: Spectral Reconstruction of EIS Images with Conditional GAN
projects.description: Compared four image reconstruction and denoising algorithms (GAN, cGAN, WGAN, and Autoencoder) for EIS solar observation images. The cGAN removes 93% of noise and improves denoising capabilities of the EIS instrument aboard the Hinode spacecraft. Model is actively deployed.

projects.title: Video Captioning with Stacked Attention
projects.description: Compared different attention mechanisms for video captioning and created a stacked attention model achieving state-of-the-art performance on the MSVD dataset. A detailed ablation study demonstrated the contribution of stacked attention in retaining semantic information.
